dossier.architecture: Dual-collector cargo cycling robot; onseason high-bar and offseason traversal configurations must be distinguished.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve-family architecture; exact module specification not established in this review.
subsystems.intake: Single collector at week 1; later opposed wide mecanum collectors supported drive-by pickup.
subsystems.transfer: Single-sided belts select upward storage or wrong-color passthrough.
subsystems.scoring: Range launcher; reviewed source establishes moving-shot virtual targeting added between second regional and Worlds. Exact hood/turret geometry remains unresolved.
subsystems.endgame: Onseason high-bar: an extension-envelope oversight compromised traversal. Reorientation before Worlds did not produce a sufficiently reliable fast traversal. Offseason added belted traversal, static hooks and pneumatic pivot.
subsystems.controls: Two-button driver workflow; opponent-cargo-only mode was implemented but reportedly never used.

versions: Onseason: dual intake and moving-shot software added.
Chezy interview shows a later traversal system, not the original Worlds climb.
dossier.analysis: The most useful lesson is the opportunity cost of endgame: a predictable high climb can outperform an unreliable traversal when alliance partners already cover the higher bars. Do not transfer the offseason climb into the Worlds performance explanation.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2022-5940 · Dual acquisition improves route flexibility without proving every component optimal
context_documents.body:
# 2022-5940: Dual acquisition improves route flexibility without proving every component optimal

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A second opposed collector was added after the single-intake early robot to support drive-by autonomous pickup. The source reports wide mecanum collectors, a controlled upward/passthrough belt path and a later moving-shot solution. The onseason climb differs from an offseason traversal upgrade.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly ties dual pickup to easier drive-by autonomous, while cautioning that its mecanum implementation required many iterations and was not a blanket recommendation.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A successful robot can contain a mechanism the team would not copy again. Preserve that negative experience. Additional pickup directions buy route freedom, but require two transport-entry cases and greater repair exposure.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Compare complete auto routes, feed/rejection recovery and the exact onseason climb; do not back-project the offseason improvement.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: Behind the Bumpers with BREAD at Chezy Champs
source_reviews.locator: 1:20–3:38 collection and passthrough; 3:40–4:52 controls and moving shots; 4:54–6:29 offseason climb
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.
facts: Dual intakes were chosen to simplify drive-by autonomous. A single-sided belt system either passes cargo straight through or raises it into storage.
Sensor-driven states reduce normal intake commands to two side selections.
The interview shows the traversal configuration. The earlier team release explains why they kept the high-bar climb during the season.
source_reviews.limitations: The Chezy interview retrospectively describes the season. Onseason code and the offseason climb are separate snapshots.

source_reviews.title: BREAD Brioche release
source_reviews.review_basis: Read team-authored release and technical reply.
facts: Publishes onseason code and CAD links. Team member explains the high-bar choice and later traversal intent.

source_reviews.title: BREAD onseason intake Java
facts: Distinct idle, acquire and reverse output with deployed or retracted modes.

source_reviews.title: BREAD onseason shooter Java
facts: Hood homing, dual setpoint checks and timed stabilization.
source_reviews.limitations: Does not establish which competition binary ran this exact snapshot.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Brioche treated both ends as entrances and gave a piece a route straight out the other end. The main benefit was keeping the driver or autonomous routine on a useful heading while collecting and rejecting. The architecture depends on the center selector pulling a wanted piece up before it travels out, and on clean sensing when either end can be the entrance.
piece_flow: Select the near-side wide intake and vector the piece toward the center.
Read the lower presence and color sensors. Move a wanted ball up to storage or pass an unwanted one through to the far side.
Upper presence sensing confirms staging. The shooter uses separate hood and flywheel targets.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The central belt path must leave both ends clear, while the upper storage and shooter sit above it. Two deployable collectors occupy both chassis edges and create two sets of service points. The team kept two climb belts inside a large tube, and the original extension exceeded the intended frame allowance according to its release.

subsystems.name: Dual intake and bidirectional selector
subsystems.construction: Two wide vectoring collectors, single-sided belts, lower color and beam-break sensing and upper beam-break sensing. Public intake code has distinct idle, acquire and reverse states with independent deployment state.
subsystems.operation: Choose intake side, then pass through or raise cargo based on sensor state.
subsystems.team_rationale: Dual entry made the planned drive-by autonomous easier. The team reports many intake iterations and expressed reservations about transferring its mecanum implementation.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Judge whether heading flexibility actually removes a turn over a complete route. Dual collection can double the service burden without doubling throughput when both mouths share one selector.
subsystems.interfaces: A staged ball must remain isolated when the floor path reverses or rejects.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test both entry directions and interruptions with a correct ball staged above a rejection.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact selector geometry, fault recovery and simultaneous-entry behavior remain unknown.

subsystems.name: Launcher and moving shot
subsystems.construction: Adjustable hood and flywheel with separate feedback checks. The onseason shooter code has homing, idle, approach, stabilization and at-setpoint states.
subsystems.operation: Shift to a virtual target based on chassis motion in the reported later strategy. In the reviewed code, enter stabilization once both setpoints agree, wait 0.25 seconds and subsequently leave ready if either drifts.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team added moving shots to reduce time spent stopping near clusters.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The stabilization timer shows why a shot can be mechanically capable yet delayed. In the reviewed state machine the timer itself does not require continuous in-tolerance feedback before entering at-setpoint. Verify the downstream feed gate before treating that as a shot authorization bug.
subsystems.interfaces: Estimated chassis velocity and launch readiness must be aligned in time.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test speed drop after a shot, a hood rehome and command changes during stabilization.
subsystems.unknowns: Release orchestration and event-deployed software were not audited.

subsystems.name: High-bar and traversal climb
subsystems.construction: Onseason belted assembly packaged two belts inside its tube. The Chezy traversal version uses static hooks, pneumatic pivot and a rear hook.
subsystems.operation: Transfer from mid to high, then catch traversal in the later version.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team cites extension overshoot in CAD and unreliable swing in a flipped pre-Champs setup. It kept high during the season and spent saved time scoring when partners could traverse.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The full envelope and success probability can outweigh extra points from nominal reach.
subsystems.interfaces: Check belt adjustment access, path interference and the reach at actual suspended attitude.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Measure stretch and alignment with unequal side loads.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact offseason changes and field success distribution remain unknown.

revisions: Single intake concept replaced by dual intake. Moving shot added before Worlds. High-bar onseason choice and later Chezy traversal remain distinct.
transferable_principles: A pass-through is valuable when it preserves travel direction.
Budget for state settling and calibration in cycle time.
disconfirming_conditions: If route geometry rarely calls for the second entrance, its mass and maintenance can outweigh time saved.
If later reach requires reliable swing that the field cannot provide, favor a lower verified climb.
remaining_gaps: Selector code, match configuration details, as-built CAD and measured throughput.

recommended_images.caption: Team release attachment. Inspect to identify installed climb configuration.
